questions.q: What direction do restriction rules work in, compared to OWD, role hierarchy, and sharing rules?
options: They narrow access a user would otherwise have — the opposite of the grant-based tools
They grant additional access on top of OWD, same as sharing rules
They replace OWD entirely
They only affect field-level security, not records
questions.explain: OWD, hierarchy, and sharing rules all grant access; restriction rules do the opposite — they filter down what a user can already see.

questions.q: A user has View All on an object at the profile level. What happens to a restriction rule defined for that user on that object?
options: It still filters their records as normal
It converts automatically into a sharing rule
It is bypassed — View All overrides restriction rules
It blocks the user from logging in
questions.explain: View All (and Modify All) bypass restriction rules entirely, since restriction rules can only narrow access, never grant or override object-level permissions like View All.

questions.q: What does a scoping rule actually change?
options: The user's real record-level access, same as a restriction rule
The org-wide default for the object
Field-level security on the object
The default scope shown in list views, lookups, and the mobile app — not underlying access
questions.explain: Scoping rules set what loads by default; the user's actual access to records outside that scope is unchanged, and they can still search for and open them.

questions.q: Why might an admin use a restriction rule on the same object where a sharing rule already grants broad access?
options: Restriction rules and sharing rules can't be used on the same object
To carve out a sliver of sensitive records that should stay hidden even though the sharing rule technically grants access
To completely disable the sharing rule
Restriction rules must always be built before any sharing rule
questions.explain: The two commonly coexist: sharing grants broad access for the general case, while a restriction rule narrows it for the specific sensitive subset.

questions.q: According to this lesson, are restriction rules available on every standard object?
options: No — they support custom objects and a specific, evolving list of standard objects, which should be confirmed in Salesforce Help before relying on one
Yes, every standard and custom object supports them identically
No, restriction rules only work on custom objects, never standard ones
They only work on Leads and Opportunities
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that the supported standard-object list is specific and has expanded release over release, so it's worth confirming currently rather than assuming.
